summary: This increment adds real, additive, client-side browser-execution engine code (WebLLM lite-llm wiring, an MCP-JSON-RPC-shaped tool-calling contract, a SharedArrayBuffer/Atomics-coordinated worker pool, Transformers.js embedding wiring, and IndexedDB model-weight caching) entirely under src/lib/browser-execution/, with two small additive dependency entries in package.json/bun.lock and no changes to migrations, schema, auth, RLS, payment/billing paths, .env files, or .github/workflows/**. I independently re-ran the claimed verification rather than trusting the self-report: `bun test src/lib/browser-execution/` reproduced exactly 58 pass/0 fail across 8 files, the full `bun test` reproduced exactly 2088 pass/0 fail across 180 files (matching PROGRESS.md's numbers), and `bunx tsc --noEmit` is clean repo-wide. Source review of webllm-engine.ts, tool-calling.ts, worker-pool.ts, and model-cache.ts shows sound, well-scoped design: tier selection stays centralized in tier-orchestrator.ts, WebLLM's model/quantization choice and its native IndexedDB cache flag are justified with real evidence, the tool-calling registry is a pure client-side contract with no wiring into any live send path yet (so no new attack surface is actually exercised), and the worker pool's SharedArrayBuffer usage and queueing logic are correct for the tested scenarios. Disclosed limitations (no live-WebGPU smoke test, no streaming, no VeriComposer wiring) are honestly scoped as future work rather than silently glossed over. This is a clean, low-blast-radius, tier1-appropriate change.
